note:
1001 -> 1066, WHICH IS A REPAIR AND A CORRECTION, NOT A CONCESSION.

The repair: `odoo/libs/worker_thread.py` and its suite carried 12 `attr-defined`
errors, every one of them `"Thread" has no attribute "dbname"`. That module
exists to give the attributes this fork bolts onto `threading.Thread` a typed
face -- the `WorkerThread` Protocol and `as_worker_thread()` -- and
`working_on_database` reached past its own facility to write `dbname` on the
bare `Thread`, so the accessor was something only OTHER modules had to use. It
and the suite now go through `as_worker_thread`, and the fixture's `had` flag
folds into `previous is not None`, which is the absent-vs-None call
`working_on_database` itself makes. 12 -> 0, `pytest odoo/libs/tests/test_worker_thread.py`
5 passed, ruff clean.

The correction: 1001 was never a number this repository produces. f4031cf8d2f
banked it, and a detached worktree AT f4031cf8d2f, measured per §9.3 -- a fresh
venv holding mypy==2.3.0 and nothing else, `--no-incremental`, the six packages
py_typecheck.yml names -- reports 1066. So the gate has been red by 65 since the
day it was set, on a tree nobody could reach, which is the second time this floor
has been banked against something uncommitted: its own note opens by describing
the first (1043 "a delta applied to a number nobody re-measured") and closes by
calling itself "AN ABSOLUTE READING, taken in the environment the gate uses".
It was not.

1066 is that reading. Measured three times, at f4031cf8d2f, at HEAD before the
worker_thread repair (1078) and at HEAD after it (1066); the whole 1078 - 1066
is the 12 errors named above, diffed file by file with no other file moving by
one. A floor that reproduces is the only kind worth having: this one does, from
a commit, with the command in §9.3.
